slides.1.title: Level 1 review
slides.1.highlights.0.title: History
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Rome → medieval still wines → 1662 Merret → the Dom Pérignon myth → 1911 riots → 1927/1936 delimitation and AOC → 2015 UNESCO
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Terroir
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Marginal northern climate, chalk (reservoir, temperature regulator, cellars), five départements (Marne largest) and four sub-regions
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Grapes and winemaking
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Three main grapes at about a third each; traditional method: base wine → tirage → bottle fermentation → lees ageing → riddling → disgorgement → dosage → closure
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Styles and labels
slides.1.highlights.3.content: NV / Vintage / Blanc de Blancs / Blanc de Noirs / Rosé; sweetness order; NM / RM / CM / RC / SR / ND / MA
slides.1.content: Figures that differ between sources (grape shares, producer counts, département shares, new-variety dates) are outside this assessment. After it, move on to Level 2.
slides.2.componentProps.slide.title: 📋 Level 1 Assessment
Which statement about Dom Pérignon and the origin of Champagne is correct?
A. He invented second fermentation in 1662
B. Bubbles were observed and recorded before him; his contribution was pressing and blending
C. He founded the UNESCO-listed cellars
D. He drew up the 1936 AOC
Merret's paper of 1662 predates his arrival; Champagne was not invented by anyone.
What base-wine character does the marginal climate most directly produce?
A. Low acid, high alcohol
B. Deep colour, heavy tannin
C. High acidity, lower sugar
D. Intense sweetness
Hard ripening keeps acidity and holds sugar down, which suits sparkling base wine.
Which two functions of chalk matter most in Champagne?
A. A water reservoir and temperature regulator, and cool stable cellars
B. Raising sugar and colour
C. Preventing mildew and replacing pruning
D. Adding tannin
Chalk stores water, buffers temperature and left the pits and tunnels used as cellars.
Which sub-region and main grape pairing is correct?
A. Côte des Bar — Chardonnay
B. Vallée de la Marne — Chardonnay
C. Montagne de Reims — Meunier
D. Côte des Blancs — Chardonnay
Côte des Blancs Chardonnay; Marne Valley Meunier; Montagne de Reims and Côte des Bar Pinot Noir.
Which grapes does Blanc de Noirs use?
A. Chardonnay only
B. Pinot Noir and/or Meunier only
C. Arbane and Petit Meslier
D. All three main grapes
Blanc de Noirs uses black grapes only; Blanc de Blancs uses white grapes only.
Which step sets the final sweetness?
A. Pressing
B. Remuage
C. The dosage (liqueur d'expédition) after disgorgement
D. The liqueur de tirage at bottling
The tirage sugar is for the bubbles; sweetness is set by the dosage added after disgorgement.
What are the minimum ageing periods (from bottling) for NV and Vintage Champagne?
A. 15 and 36 months
B. 12 and 24 months
C. 9 and 18 months
D. 36 and 60 months
NV needs at least 15 months and Vintage at least 36.
On a label, what do NM and RM mean?
A. Cooperative and buyer's brand
B. Vintage and non-vintage
C. A grower-producer and a house
D. A house (négociant) and a grower-producer (récoltant)
NM is Négociant-Manipulant (a house) and RM is Récoltant-Manipulant (a grower).
